title: The Old Cow at the Gate
logline: At dusk a herder drives the cattle into the pen; at dawn he opens the gate, and it is never the strongest animal that leaves first, it is whoever ended up nearest the door.
human_question: Does what matters most always come first, or just what is closest to hand?

situation.what_happens: A herder brings his animals in at dusk, settles the disputes over space that happen every night, and opens the gate again at dawn. He knows each animal individually and can say which is strong, which is old and which is trouble. When the gate opens, the order they come out in is decided by where they happen to be standing.
situation.who_is_involved: A working herder whose income depends on the animals; the household that shares the labour; and neighbours who use the same pen or the same grazing.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A season's income and the condition of the animals, and for the film the honesty of not bending real animal behaviour to fit an old comparison.
situation.how_it_unfolds: The cycle is the same every day and the variation is all in weather, feed and which animals are calving or ailing. Reality decides what happens at the gate, and if the animals do not behave as the comparison suggests, that is what the film has.

concept_merge.why_together: One concept only. The order of ripening (C056) says which action gives the next rebirth: weighty first, then what is done or recalled near the end, then what is habitual, then whatever is left over. The source illustrates this with an old, weak cow that leaves the pen first because it is nearest the gate.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: How ordering differs from weight, and also how little a single image can carry: the source's own sentence here is compressed enough that the digest asks for an expert reading of it before anyone relies on it.

concept_links.why: The source illustrates the ordering of results with an old, weak cow that leaves the pen first because it is nearest the gate [C056-P:L119]. The earlier version of this link said the image shows that what is nearest the end outweighs what is strongest in a life, which the sources do not say: weighty action takes priority over everything, and what is near death decides only where there is no weighty action [C056-P:L117]. The digest also flags this very line as syntactically compressed, with two possible readings, and asks for an expert check, so the image cannot carry a film by itself. The digest's warning that the source's examples of habitual occupations must never be used to frame working communities applies here too.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Which of a life's actions gives the next rebirth is settled by an order, weighty first, then what is near the end, then what is habitual, and not simply by which action was biggest.
what_must_be_real: A working herder's real routine, never a routine arranged to match a comparison. If the animals do not do what the old image says, the film follows the animals.
position_hint: middle, if it were kept: an image-led film with no human situation of its own, which is why its concept has been folded into a film that has one.
risks: Staging animal behaviour to force the comparison
Presenting a line the digest flags for expert checking as settled doctrine
drop_if: The animals' actual behaviour contradicts the image and the film cannot use it honestly
No working herder will allow overnight filming

connections.note: The ordering of results now sits in the film about being called to a bedside, where it has a human situation, and the correction to the old why travels with it.
A gate and a ledger are two everyday images for the same family of ideas about what comes due and when.

selection.reason: Its concept is already carried by an episode, its why was inaccurate, and its one image rests on a line the digest flags for expert checking.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
